newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on primary rate forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on primary rate forecast.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 80 basis points on Tuesday at a session high of 22.80 percent, in line with increased estimates of primary rates to be assigned later in the day, traders said.
"The market is still skittish and closely watching the U.S. bond market. (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan speaks tomorrow, and it all keeps the pressure on," a trader said.
"Term rates seesawed a lot today, albeit at light trade. Betting on the outcome of the primary auction spurred volatility," he added.
A Reuters survey nN04550765 of eight money market traders in Mexico City showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day rates at an average of 21.61 percent.
This would be an increase of 302 basis points from last week's auction.
Auction results are expected at 1830 local time/0030 GMT.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts reversed initial firmness to close 0.2 of a centavo weaker at 7.9930/7.9970 per dollar.
Traders said the late slide in the peso fueled forecast assignment rates for primary 28-day Cetes.
"At one stage dealers thought the hike would be just 200 basis points, but estimates rose as the peso flagged. Some are even expecting a rise of 350 basis points," another trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 20 basis points at 23.90 percent.
The central bank drained 1.886 billion pesos from the secondary market through three auctions, which it assigned at rates of between 24.01-24.13 percent, and maturities of between one and 16 days.

Traders said Mexican financial markets for the rest of the week would in general closely follow developments in yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, which stood at 6.87 percent in late trade, up from 6.82 earlier in the day.
Liquidity of 950 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
